outcome.summary: Partial result only; the all-orders conjecture remains open. The result is conditional on these imported premises: Kantor (1987), which depends on the classification of finite simple groups; the Thas–Zagier identification of the remaining case with D=μ_(n+1) in F_p, the necessity of 2^(n+1)≡1 (mod p), and their n<2×10^11 computation; and Feit's valid conditions 8|n and d^(n+1)≡1 (mod p) for every divisor d of n, which give n≡8 (mod 24). Under these premises, an exact Python recomputation, replayed in the no-network sandbox, eliminates every n≡8 (mod 24) in [200000000000, 251539607552). Each member has either a proper prime factor q≤10^6 of p=n²+n+1 or 2^(n+1)≢1 (mod p), and there are no survivors. Hence no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane of order n<251539607552 exists. Tw
